h1: Gallery Design Hotel Sisaket — A Boutique with a Pool and a Great Breakfast Near the Railway Station
intro: If you arrive in Sisaket by train and want more than a bare room — somewhere with an outdoor pool and a genuinely good breakfast at a price that still makes sense — Gallery Design Hotel comes up again and again in reviews. The one thing guests mention most is the buffet breakfast, which many call the best of their whole Isan trip, plus an outdoor pool you rarely find at this price. It sits on Ubon Road in the city centre, about 800 m from Sisaket railway station, within a short walk of Wat Maha Phuttharam and the Fountain Circle. There are 28 rooms, free parking, an EV charging point and free bicycles, with rates from approximately ฿1,000/night. It scores 9.4 from 48 reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: Gallery Design Hotel is a 28-room boutique hotel in central Sisaket, on Ubon Road in Mueang Tai, near the railway station. It opened in 2016 and was renovated in 2021. What sets it apart from the usual city hotels here is that it cares about design and has an outdoor pool — something you rarely find in Sisaket at this price point. It is a SHA Extra Plus property, so cleanliness follows the national health-and-safety standard.

Rooms range from Superior (twin beds) up to Deluxe with a king bed and the larger Exclusive. The thing guests agree on is that the rooms are spacious and clean, with good-quality linens and towels, and the Wi-Fi is fast. Every room has air-con, a fridge and a flat-screen TV. Several staff speak English, which makes it easy for the foreign travellers passing through southern Isan. Everything in the room is functional and well matched to the price.
"Clean room, strong Wi-Fi, and the best breakfast we had at any hotel in Thailand. The staff were friendly and really helpful."

The single most talked-about feature is the buffet breakfast at Showlo Restaurant — Thai dishes, bread, eggs cooked to order and a coffee machine. Many guests say it is better than they expected for a hotel this size. There is also the outdoor pool, a sauna, massage service and free bicycles for getting around town. One nice touch: the hotel has an EV charging point, still rare in Sisaket, which is handy if you are touring southern Isan in an electric car.

Location is another reason people choose it. It is right in the city centre, about 800 m from Sisaket railway station — a short walk or quick ride. Wat Maha Phuttharam (the temple of the big standing Buddha) and the Fountain Circle are roughly 10 minutes on foot. There are restaurants, convenience stores and a market nearby, so finding food is easy, and there is plenty of free parking for guests arriving by train or by car.

To be straight about it, based on real guest reviews: the most common note is that the beds are on the firm side for some people, and a few find the decor a touch loud or starting to look dated in places. There are occasional mentions of a musty smell in some rooms and a fiddly tap. One thing worth knowing is that the pool is on the far side of the car park, so you have to walk across to reach it rather than it being right by the rooms. English-language TV channels are limited.

In short, if you want a city hotel in Sisaket with a pool, a good breakfast and some design character, at a low-four-figure baht price near the railway station, Gallery Design Hotel is a sensible pick. Its 9.4 from 48 reviews on Trip.com, plus a TripAdvisor ranking of #2 of 7 Sisaket hotels, reflect the consensus well: clean, great breakfast, friendly service. It suits train travellers, EV drivers and anyone who wants a pool on a budget.

A tip from reading the reviews here: if you really prefer a soft mattress, mention the firm beds at check-in and ask for a topper or a different room. And do not miss the buffet breakfast early (it runs 6:30–10:00 am), since it is the most praised part of the stay. If you are arriving by train, let the hotel know in advance — they offer a station transfer.

You just have to accept that the beds are fairly firm, the decor looks dated in places, and the pool means a walk across the car park.
honestChecks: If you mainly sleep on a soft mattress — several reviews call the beds firm → ask for a mattress topper or a different room at check-in.

If you expect crisp, brand-new design everywhere — the hotel was renovated in 2021 but some corners look dated and the styling is bold → if you prefer modern minimalism, look at another city boutique.
If you plan to mainly use the pool — it sits on the far side of the car park, not next to the rooms → factor in the walk, though a pool is still rare at this price.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Gallery Design Hotel Sisaket

faq.q: Where is Gallery Design Hotel in Sisaket and what is nearby?
faq.a: Gallery Design Hotel is on Ubon Road in Mueang Tai, central Sisaket, near the railway station (about 800 m away). It is roughly a 10-minute walk to Wat Maha Phuttharam (the temple of the big standing Buddha) and the Fountain Circle, with restaurants, convenience stores and a market around the hotel for easy meals.

faq.q: How much does Gallery Design Hotel cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at approximately ฿1,000/night for a Superior Twin. Deluxe King and Exclusive rooms run around ฿1,100–฿1,400, with family rooms higher. Prices vary by season — always compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does Gallery Design Hotel have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — both an outdoor pool and a buffet breakfast. The breakfast at Showlo Restaurant is the most praised part of the stay, running 6:30–10:00 am with Thai dishes, bread and eggs to order. The pool sits on the far side of the car park, so you walk across to reach it.

faq.q: Who is Gallery Design Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits travellers who want a city boutique in Sisaket with a pool and a good breakfast at a low-four-figure baht price. It works well for train travellers, EV drivers and couples or small families who want a pool. If you strongly prefer a soft bed, ask for a topper at check-in.

faq.q: Does Gallery Design Hotel have EV charging?
faq.a: Yes — the hotel has an EV charging point, still rare in Sisaket, plus plenty of free parking. It is handy for anyone driving an electric car around southern Isan who needs to charge during their stay.

faq.q: Are the rooms clean and quiet at Gallery Design Hotel?
faq.a: Most reviews confirm the rooms are spacious and clean, with good linens and fast Wi-Fi. Worth knowing: the beds are firm for some guests, a few rooms have a musty smell, and the decor looks dated in places — so check the room when you arrive.
